title: One Rod Change Doubled the Load on This Walkway
cta: Which link should have been caught first? Tell us in the comments

facts.label: Year the Hyatt Regency walkways collapsed
Day of July 1981 the walkways collapsed
Hour of the collapse (p.m.), approximately 7:05 p.m.
Minutes past the hour of the collapse (approximately 7:05 p.m.)
People left dead by the collapse (NBS executive summary)
Ultimate capacity of the original continuous-rod connection, percent of that expected under the Kansas City Building Code (approximately)
How many times the rod change multiplied the load on the fourth-floor box beam-hanger rod connections (essentially doubled)
Year ASCE adopted the policy assigning responsibility for steel connection design to the engineer of record (October 1985)
People injured in the collapse (NBS executive summary)
People on the second and fourth floor walkways at the collapse (NBS credible estimate from a news videotape)
Maximum load on a fourth floor box beam-hanger rod connection at the collapse, percent of the ultimate capacity expected under the Kansas City Building Code
Hanger rods suspending the fourth floor walkway from the atrium roof framing
Year the Hyatt Regency Kansas City opened (July 1980)
Inches the second-to-fourth floor rod was offset inward along the box beam (4 in, 102 mm)
Minimum ultimate load a fourth floor box beam-hanger rod connection should have supported under the code, kN (68 kips)
Average ultimate capacity estimated for the six fourth floor walkway connections, kN (18.6 kips)
Actual walkway dead load above the nominal dead load, percent (approximately)
Day of July 1981 the NBS researchers first arrived in Kansas City
Third floor walkway connection under the original detail, percent of the expected ultimate capacity (approximately)
Depth in inches of the steel channels (MC8) paired into each box beam
Crowd in the atrium area at 7:00 PM, low estimate (NBS timeline from the Kansas City Times/Star)
Crowd in the atrium area at 7:00 PM, high estimate (NBS timeline)
Minutes past 7 PM the band returned from its break to play for a dance contest (7:04 PM, NBS timeline)
Minutes past 7 PM the fire department dispatcher received the first call for help (7:08 PM, NBS timeline)

beats.say: The Hyatt Regency hotel in Kansas City, July {fact2}, {fact1}. Two walkways hang above a packed atrium.

params.place: the Hyatt Regency atrium, early evening

moments.what: the hotel name types on under the date caption over the lit atrium
the camera glides in under the glass roof trusses
the fourth- and second-floor walkways light along their edges
labels draw to both walkways
the dance floor glows warm and pulses below

params.caption: date

beats.say: At {fact4} past {fact3} in the evening, the upper walkway gives way.

params.place: inside the fourth-floor box beam, then the atrium

moments.what: a clock reading the time appears beside the beam cutaway
the nut under the beam glows amber, then red
the seam splits and the nut pulls through the beam
cut wide: the upper walkway drops

beats.say: It drops onto the walkway below it, and both fall into the crowd below.

moments.what: the upper walkway lands on the lower one
both walkways fall to the floor and dust rises
the dance-floor lights go dark under the dust

beats.say: It wasn't bad steel or bad workmanship that started it. The federal report says so.

params.place: the federal investigation report on a desk

moments.what: a steel sample tag stamps RULED OUT
a workmanship tag stamps RULED OUT
the report page slides in and its line highlights

beats.say: It took a weak detail, a change in how the rods were hung, and a review that let it through.

params.place: the cause chain on the investigation board

moments.what: a status lamp lights as the second link draws
the first link writes on: weak detail
the second link: one rod changed
the third link: a review let it through
the chain glows red end to end

beats.say: Here is the hotel, the design, the change, the last minutes, the failure, the findings, and what changed after.

moments.what: chapter one lights on the panel
chapter two lights
chapter three lights
chapter four lights
chapter five lights red
chapter six lights
chapter seven lights and the title stamps on

beats.say: The Hyatt Regency opened in {fact13}, a new tower hotel in downtown Kansas City.

params.place: the street outside the hotel at dusk

moments.what: the sign on the forecourt lights with the opening year
the camera tilts up the lit tower

beats.say: Its showpiece was a tall atrium, roofed in glass, between the tower and the meeting rooms.

moments.what: the camera rises over the hotel
the atrium roof glows
the tower outline lights
the meeting-room block outline lights

beats.say: Three walkways crossed it, on the second, third and fourth floors.

moments.what: the camera drifts across the atrium
the second-floor walkway lights
the third-floor walkway lights
the fourth-floor walkway lights

beats.say: The third floor walkway ran off to one side, on its own rods.

moments.what: the third-floor walkway lights alone
the camera slides along it
its own rods to the roof light up

beats.say: The fourth floor walkway ran directly above the second.

moments.what: the fourth-floor walkway lights
a plumb line drops between them
the second-floor walkway lights beneath

beats.say: No columns stood under them. They hung from the roof on steel rods.

params.place: the empty floor under the walkways

moments.what: ghost columns appear under the walkways and are struck out
the camera tilts up
the roof trusses light
the hanger rods glow from roof to walkway

beats.say: The fourth floor walkway hung from {fact12} rods, tied into the roof framing.

params.place: at the atrium roof, by the rod brackets

moments.what: the camera follows the rods up from the fourth-floor walkway
the rods count off one by one on a tag
a rod bracket on the roof truss lights

beats.say: That Friday, the hotel held a dance in the atrium.

moments.what: the date card flips to Friday
the bandstand lights come up
the floor lights pulse in time

beats.say: By early evening, the crowd was estimated at {fact21} to {fact22} people.

params.place: the atrium floor from the terrace

moments.what: table lamps come on across the floor
a counter on the terrace column counts up to the estimate
the floor fills with warm light

beats.say: Some watched from the walkways. Why did that matter? For that, we need the drawings.

moments.what: the walkway outline glows on the sheet
the lamp swings over the table
a rolled drawing unrolls across the table

beats.say: Each walkway rested on steel box beams, laid across underneath its deck.

moments.what: the deck lifts away in cutaway
three box beams light under it
the camera ducks under the deck

beats.say: Each box beam was two {fact20}-inch steel channels, welded toe to toe into a hollow box.

moments.what: two channels slide in from either side
a weld bead runs along the seam with sparks
the camera looks down the hollow box

beats.say: A hanger rod passed down through holes in the beam.

moments.what: the rod lowers from above
it threads through the holes in both flanges

beats.say: Under the beam sat a washer and a nut. The beam simply rested on them.

params.place: under the box beam, at the nut

moments.what: the washer slides up the rod
the nut spins on
the beam settles onto the nut and a force arrow presses down

beats.say: In the original design, one long rod ran from the roof, through the fourth floor beam, down to the second.

params.place: the original drawing on the light table

moments.what: the original sheet slides in
one long rod draws from the roof
it passes through the fourth-floor beam
and on to the second-floor beam

beats.say: Each beam had its own nut on that rod, so each carried only its own walkway.

params.place: the original drawing on the light table

moments.what: both nuts pulse
one load arrow appears on each beam
each beam gets a one-walkway tag

beats.say: The rod carried both walkways. Each nut held just one.

params.place: the original drawing on the light table

moments.what: the upper rod segment glows thick
the arrows add up the rod
the fourth-floor nut is ringed: one walkway

beats.say: Sounds solid, doesn't it? Investigators later tested that original connection in a lab.

moments.what: a beam mock-up sits in the steel test frame
the ram lowers onto the rod
the lab lights come up

beats.say: It would have had only about {fact6} of the strength the building code expected.

moments.what: the original bar starts to rise; a status lamp lights
the code bar fills to its mark
the original connection bar stops well short, at its figure

beats.say: So where was the weak spot? The beam. Its thin edges could bend round the washer and split along the weld.

params.place: under the box beam, at the nut

moments.what: the camera settles on the bottom flange; a status lamp lights
the flange around the washer warms amber
the edges flex upward
a red line runs along the weld

beats.say: So the walkways began with less margin than the code required. Then the design changed.

moments.what: a red pencil circles the connection
an eraser wipes the long rod off the sheet

beats.say: Who decides exactly how each part is made? The steel fabricator, in its shop drawings.

moments.what: a status lamp lights as the sheets settle
a stack of sheets drops onto the table
the fabricator's title block lights
the title block types SHOP DRAWING

beats.say: Those drawings used two rods instead of one long one.

moments.what: two short rods draw on
the long rod is struck through

beats.say: One rod hung the fourth floor beam from the roof.

moments.what: the upper rod draws
the fourth-floor beam hangs on it
it ties to the roof

beats.say: A second rod, set {fact14} inches inward, hung the second floor beam from the fourth floor beam.

moments.what: the second-floor beam outline brightens; a status lamp lights
the lower rod draws
a dimension tag shows the offset
the second-floor beam hangs from the fourth-floor beam

beats.say: As reported, the fabricator asked the engineers about the change by phone, and it was approved verbally.

moments.what: an AS REPORTED tag sits on the frame
the desk phone rings, its bell shaking
the receiver lifts
a speech line types APPROVED

beats.say: The engineering firm later disputed that call.

moments.what: the receiver goes back down
a DISPUTED stamp slams beside the phone

beats.say: But the shop drawings came back stamped as reviewed, by the contractor, the engineer and the architect.

moments.what: the sheet slides back onto the table
the contractor stamp lands
the engineer stamp lands
the architect stamp lands

beats.say: On paper, a rod had moved a few inches.

params.place: the two drawings side by side

moments.what: the original and the shop detail slide side by side
the rod position shifts
a small gap tag pops

beats.say: So what really changed? In the steel, the weight now took a different path.

moments.what: the drawing goes dark
load arrows appear on the lower walkway
the arrows travel up the lower rod into the upper beam

beats.say: The lower walkway no longer hung from the roof. It hung from the upper walkway's beams.

moments.what: the second-floor walkway lights
the old long rods fade
the short rods to the upper beams glow

beats.say: So the nut under each fourth floor beam carried the upper walkway, and the lower one as well.

params.place: under the fourth-floor box beam, cut away

moments.what: the nut is ringed
one load arrow presses on the beam
a second arrow joins it from the lower rod

beats.say: How much more? Those connections now carried {fact7} times the load of the original design.

moments.what: the load needle sits at one walkway
the needle swings to double and the dial turns amber

beats.say: A connection that was already weak now had double the work. And the crowd was coming.

params.place: the atrium floor before the dance

moments.what: the fourth-floor beams glow amber
both walkways light together
the floor lights come on, warm

beats.say: Friday, July {fact2}. People begin arriving for the dance in the afternoon.

moments.what: the date reel rolls to Friday
the crowd meter starts to climb
the sun lamp on the panel glows

beats.say: Seats fill up, and people start to gather on the walkways to watch.

moments.what: table lamps fill the floor
warm light gathers along the walkway decks
the camera tracks along the rail

beats.say: A television news crew was there, filming the dance.

params.place: the news camera on the terrace

moments.what: the news camera swings round
the REC light blinks and the viewfinder fills the frame

beats.say: From that tape, investigators estimated up to {fact10} people on the second and fourth floor walkways.

moments.what: a status lamp lights as the count runs
a videotape slides into the deck
the frame freezes and a count tag ticks up
both walkways are outlined on the frozen frame

beats.say: Too many people? No. That was far less weight than the walkways were designed to carry.

moments.what: a status lamp lights as the needle settles low
the crowd load needle rises a little
the design-load mark lights far above it

beats.say: At {fact23} past {fact3}, the band returns from its break for a dance contest.

moments.what: the clock ticks to the time
the band lamp on the panel lights
the floor meter pulses

beats.say: Which connection would go first? Under the fourth floor walkway, any one of them could.

moments.what: the camera slides under the fourth-floor walkway
each connection glows amber in turn
the middle one glows hotter

beats.say: Yet the load on them reached, at most, only {fact11} of what a connection built to code should hold.

moments.what: the gauge wakes, needle at zero
the load needle rises
it stops at the figure
the scale lights up to the top
the code mark lights far above it
the gap between them glows

beats.say: From the day they were built, the report found, the walkways could barely hold their own weight.

params.place: the atrium from the roof, looking down

moments.what: a status lamp lights; the quote finishes typing
the camera looks straight down on the walkways
a quote line types on
the walkway decks pulse amber

quote.text: MINIMAL CAPACITY TO RESIST THEIR OWN WEIGHT

beats.say: How long did it hold? Moments after the band came back, the first connection gave way.

moments.what: the band lamp flickers
the second hand sweeps
the band lamp blinks
every lamp on the panel goes red

beats.say: It began at the east end of the fourth floor walkway's middle box beam.

moments.what: the camera dives toward the fourth-floor walkway
an EAST arrow points along the beam
the middle box beam's east end is ringed red

beats.say: The beam's lower edges bent up around the washer. The weld along the bottom split open.

params.place: inside the middle box beam, cut away

moments.what: the seam line runs red; a status lamp lights
the bottom flange warms grey to amber
the edges fold up around the washer
the weld seam tears open, red

beats.say: The rod and its nut pulled straight through the beam.

params.place: inside the middle box beam, cut away

moments.what: silence; the nut glows red
sub-boom: the nut tears through the flange with sparks
the beam drops past the nut

beats.say: Its load jumped to the connections beside it. They failed too.

moments.what: red pulses run along the walkway to the next beams
the neighbouring connections flare red
the walkway sags at the middle

beats.say: The fourth floor walkway swung down onto the second floor walkway.

moments.what: the upper walkway rotates down
it lands on the lower walkway

beats.say: Then both fell onto the lobby floor.

moments.what: both walkways drop
dust rises across the floor and the lights die

beats.say: The roof rods were left hanging, empty.

params.place: under the roof, after the collapse

moments.what: the camera tilts up from the dust
the empty rods swing
one rod end, its nut gone, fills the frame

beats.say: At {fact24} past {fact3}, the fire department took the first call for help.

moments.what: the clock ticks forward
the dispatch lamp lights and the line types FIRST CALL

beats.say: Rescuers worked through the night to free people trapped beneath the walkways.

params.place: the atrium at night, under work lights

moments.what: work lights switch on round the fallen walkways
the glass roof goes dark
the camera holds, slow and quiet

beats.say: {fact5} people died, and {fact9} were injured.

moments.what: the picture dims and a quiet line types the toll
the second line types under it

beats.say: In loss of life and injuries, the report called it the most devastating structural collapse ever in the United States.

moments.what: the summary page slides in
the sentence highlights line by line

beats.say: Why did it happen? Days later, federal investigators arrived to find out.

moments.what: the camera pushes toward the dark atrium glass
a federal van pulls up under the canopy

beats.say: The National Bureau of Standards team reached Kansas City on July {fact18}.

moments.what: the file folder opens
an arrival date stamps on the first sheet

beats.say: They weighed fallen spans and cut out beams, rods and nuts to study.

params.place: the warehouse where the debris was kept

moments.what: a span lowers onto the scale
a beam section lifts away
a rod lifts away
a nut drops into an evidence tray

beats.say: The walkways weighed about {fact17} more than the drawings estimated, a small difference.

moments.what: the scale readout counts
the drawing estimate shows beside it
a small gap tag shows the figure

beats.say: In the lab, they built copies of the connection and loaded them until they failed.

moments.what: a mock-up slides into the frame
the ram presses down and the gauge climbs
the flange folds and the gauge drops

beats.say: Under the code, each fourth floor connection should have held at least {fact15} kilonewtons.

moments.what: the code bar rises
it locks at its figure

beats.say: The tests put them at about {fact16} kilonewtons on average.

moments.what: the tested bar rises beside it
it stops far short, red

beats.say: The finding: the connections did not have enough load capacity.

moments.what: the conclusion page slides in
the line highlights

beats.say: Why so little? Two factors. The original detail was too weak, and the rod change doubled its load.

moments.what: the board lights
card one stamps CAUSE
card two stamps CAUSE

beats.say: Bad steel, or bad welding? Neither the workmanship nor the materials started it.

moments.what: a workmanship card stamps RULED OUT
a materials card stamps RULED OUT

beats.say: And a twist. With the original rods, the third floor walkway would have been the weakest, at about {fact19}.

moments.what: the third-floor walkway lights; a status lamp lights
the camera swings to the third-floor walkway
long rods ghost back in
its connections glow amber and a tag shows the figure

beats.say: So who was responsible for designing one small connection?

moments.what: the lamp swings over the table
the connection detail fills the frame under a red circle

beats.say: What happened to the engineers? Missouri's licensing board revoked the licences of two of them, for gross negligence and misconduct.

moments.what: the hearing table lights; a status lamp lights
two licence cards slide onto the table
REVOKED stamps on both
the charges type beneath

beats.say: Their professional society, ASCE, answered with a policy in {fact8}.

moments.what: the policy document slides in
its title and year stamp on

beats.say: The engineer of record is responsible for the whole steel design, connections included.

moments.what: a status lamp lights as the highlight runs
the line highlights
the word connections is underlined in red

beats.say: Under that policy, a connection is never left between the designer and the fabricator.

params.place: between the designer's and fabricator's drawings

moments.what: the connection detail sits in the gap
the designer sheet slides over it
the fabricator sheet follows, the detail now signed

beats.say: On the night they fell, the load on those connections was at most {fact11} of what the code expected them to hold.

params.place: the atrium, the night of the dance

moments.what: the atrium returns, lit and full
the camera begins its slow push
the fourth-floor connections glow amber
the middle connection pulses brighter
the code mark lights on the tag
a tag on the walkway shows the figure against the code mark

beats.say: A weak detail. A rod moved {fact14} inches. A review that let it through.

moments.what: the first link stamps CAUSE
the second link stamps CAUSE
the third link stamps FACTOR

beats.say: Which link should have been caught first? Tell us in the comments.

params.place: the Hyatt Regency atrium, early evening

moments.what: the three links hang over the atrium as tags
the camera pulls back
it settles on the opening frame of the walkways

params.cta: Which link should have been caught first?
params.assumption: From the National Bureau of Standards walkway investigation and ASCE Civil Engineering. The scenes are reconstructions, not actual footage.

thumbnails.pattern: big serious type over one document picture, the key line circled

references.what: big serious serif type over one picture of the scene
huge spaced type over one picture of the atrium
